snapshot.about: Incorporated in 2008, Kaynes Technology is a leading end-to-end and IoT solutions-enabled integrated electronics manufacturing company. The company provides conceptual design, process engineering, integrated manufacturing, and life-cycle support for major players in the automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, outer-space, nuclear, medical, railways, Internet of Things ("IoT"), Information Technology ("IT") and other segments. [1]

guidance.statement: We will start generating revenue from PCB Unit 1 from Q3 FY27.
guidance.quote: On PCB Unit 1, we will start generating revenue from Q3 FY27 itself.
guidance.speaker: Muthukumar N.

guidance.statement: We will not go for a QIP for the next one year.
guidance.quote: For the next one year, I can assure you, we will not go.
guidance.speaker: Muthukumar N.

guidance.statement: Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai will be operational by Q3 FY27.
guidance.quote: Both Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on the track to be operational by quarter 3 FY27
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Profitability will take a couple of quarters to normalize and return to earlier committed levels.
guidance.quote: We expect this could take a couple of quarters for profitability to normalize and return to the levels as we had earlier committed to.
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: Revenue starts in OSAT and PCB businesses from the third quarter.
guidance.quote: As far as OSAT and PCB is concerned, we already told from third quarter the revenue starts in both the business
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: Capex for the year is planned at INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and INR250 crores for EMS.
guidance.quote: We said we will be funding for this capex for this year is about INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and about INR250 crores for EMS business.
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: NPD-led and value-added solutions will increase to nearly 30% of total revenue in the coming years.
guidance.quote: goal is to steadily increase the contribution of NPD-led and value-added solutions to nearly 30% of the total revenue in the coming years.
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: The company commits to doubling the market growth rate going forward.
guidance.quote: So we are committing at doubling the growth of market growth, which we will be definitely coming back in every quarter
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: Rail business is expected to grow by around 20% to 25% this year.
guidance.quote: rail business, I'm expecting this year to grow by around 20%, 25% because of these coming in.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Rail business margins are going to be north of 30% plus.
guidance.quote: And the margins are going to be north of current 30% plus.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: We are still sticking to our projection of achieving $1 billion in revenue.
guidance.quote: We are only saying that we will be away from the AMISP business.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Expect at least INR1,500 crores from the OSAT business and INR1,000 crores from PC Board.
guidance.quote: So, at the minimum, you can expect INR1,500 crores from our OSAT business. Similarly, you can expect about INR1,000 crores from PC Board business.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: The company will definitely be operating cash flow positive by the end of this year.
guidance.quote: And going forward, at consol level, we'll definitely be OCF positive by end of this year.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: We will spend about another INR400-odd crores of capex this year.
guidance.quote: So you can take broadly in this year, maybe about another INR400-odd crores of capex will be spent.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: Market demand is high for the next 4, 5 years with year-on-year growth around 30%.
guidance.quote: So the market demand is so high for the next 4, 5 years, year-on-year, there will be a growth of around 30%.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Margins can go up by about 5 to 7 percentage points going forward.
guidance.quote: It can go up by about 5%, 7 percentage points going forward.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: Next few years CAGR will be similar to the last 4 years CAGR.
guidance.quote: If you take last several 4 years CAGR, the next few years CAGR also will be thereabouts.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

narrative_vs_numbers.management_says: Margins are expected to expand or normalize upwards.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers_say: Operating profit margins declined to 13% in Sep 2026 from 16% in Sep 2025.

promises.credibility: Management maintains an optimistic long-term growth narrative, but near-term margin delivery has deteriorated as evidenced by falling OPM in recent quarters.

bull: Margins are expanding with an OPM of 16% compared to the 13% average of prior years.
Profit is outgrowing revenue, showing a 3-year PAT CAGR of 56% versus 48% for revenue.
Growth capacity is underway with CWIP currently at 34% of fixed assets, though not yet earning.
bear: Growth is slowing as the 5-year revenue CAGR of 54% dropped to 48% over 3 years.
Working capital is stretching significantly, with the cash conversion cycle increasing from 123 to 193 days.
Free cash flow is negative, totaling ₹-3,288 Cr and remaining negative in all 5 of 5 years.
